rationale: At the 8.59 ns floor, AREA 3 runs keep +0.8 to +1.8 ns slack, so setup repair never engages: T_eff is natural path delay. With timing-driven placement off and no repair, the clock target only changes port delays, not the physical result. Blabla's reg-to-reg path (6.62 ns) beat round 1 (6.76), which also changed slew 39->40 and margins; at 8.59 ns its I/O path (~6.4 ns) no longer limits. Setting 1 is blabla unchanged except period_frac 0.45, to reproduce 6.62. Setting 2 keeps that recipe but turns off routability-driven inflation (routing converges in 4 iterations, congestion mild) to compact the datapath, and raises cap repair to 30% (R2-3's 12% was slower).
